subject.title: fix(stream): recover visible content when reasoning_delta straddles an inline code span (closes #96869)

question: Should native reasoning_content be recovered as visible text when it appears to close an unclosed visible inline-code span, and if so should that recovery flow through the partitioner as the canonical state owner?
rationale: This is a real message-loss bug, but the repair crosses the private reasoning versus visible answer boundary, so the permanent routing rule should be maintainer-confirmed rather than inferred from this partial guard.

options.title: Require canonical partitioner routing
options.body: Revise both stream paths so recovered visible text updates the partitioner state, cover the same-chunk case, and merge only with real after-fix provider proof.

options.title: Accept partial recovery only
options.body: Maintainers could land a narrower cross-chunk mitigation, but the linked issue should remain open for the same-chunk message-loss case.

options.title: Replace the branch
options.body: If the dirty fork is not worth repairing, ask for or create a narrow replacement that preserves credit and ports the fix to the current packages/ai layout.

recommendation.title: Require canonical partitioner routing
recommendation.body: Revise both stream paths so recovered visible text updates the partitioner state, cover the same-chunk case, and merge only with real after-fix provider proof.

likelyOwner.reason: He merged the closest recent native-reasoning boundary changes and the current path-owning PR, so he is the best available routing owner for the behavior choice.
